name: Confrontation
overview: Scripture teaches that confrontation among believers is necessary to address sin and restore relationships, as seen in commands to rebuke neighbors without hatred (Leviticus 19:17) and to address faults privately to gain a brother (Matthew 18:15). True biblical confrontation involves self-examination to avoid hypocrisy (Matthew 7:3) and is marked by gentleness and humility, restoring the fallen in a spirit of meekness (Galatians 6:1). The example of Paul confronting Peter openly for wrongdoing (Galatians 2:11) demonstrates that confrontation is sometimes direct and necessary for correction and growth within the body of Christ.
